target.title: fix(codex): use UTF-16-safe truncation for approval display paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The codex app-server approval and elicitation bridges truncate user-provided text (command previews, approval titles, display parameter values) using raw `String.prototype.slice`. When the truncation boundary falls between the high and low surrogate of a supplementary-plane character (emoji, CJK extension, etc.), the output contains a lone surrogate — corrupted UTF-16.

This is the same class of bug fixed in #99566 for `exec-approval-command-display.ts`. The shared `truncateUtf16Safe` / `sliceUtf16Safe` helpers (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`) already back off from split surrogate pairs at the boundary; they are used by 20+ other extensions but were not yet adopted in these three codex bridge files.

Relates to gap finding: `codex-utf16-safe-truncation` (`utf16-boundary`, evidence level A)
Location: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/approval-bridge.ts:1498`

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace raw `String.prototype.slice` with `truncateUtf16Safe` / `sliceUtf16Safe` in all 6 call sites across 3 source files:

| File | Function | Cap | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `truncate()` | 48–180 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `previewSource()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `approval-bridge.ts` | `appendPreviewPart()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `elicitation-bridge.ts` | `sanitizeDisplayText()` | 4096 | `value.slice(0, 4096)` → `sliceUtf16Safe(value, 0, 4096)` |
| `elicitation-bridge.ts` | `truncateDisplayText()` | 120 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |
| `plugin-approval-roundtrip.ts` | `truncateForGateway()` | 80, 256 | `slice(0, max-3)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(value, max-3)` |

The SDK helpers are dependency-free, already exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, and already in use within the same extension (`node-cli-sessions.ts:698`). Cap sizes, truncation markers, and redaction order are unchanged.

## User Impact

Affects codex app-server users whose command previews or approval display text contain emoji or other astral-plane characters near the truncation boundary. Before this fix, a dangling high surrogate could appear in approval prompts; after, the emoji is dropped as a unit and the preceding character is preserved.

## Evidence

### 1. Standalone proof script — 18 boundary tests, 0 failures

Runs the exact same UTF-16-safe algorithm (inlined from `src/shared/utf16-slice.ts`) against all 6 real call-site caps, comparing old (raw slice) vs. new (safe slice) output:

```bash
node extensions/codex/src/app-server/approval-utf16-proof.mjs
```

```
======================================================================
UTF-16-safe truncation proof — Codex app-server display paths
======================================================================

── Test 1: truncate() approval command preview (max=180) ──
  Input: 182 chars, emoji at indices 176-177
  Legacy (raw slice): 180 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 179 chars — ✅ CLEAN

── Test 2: previewSource() scan cap (max=4096) ──
  Input: 4101 chars, emoji at indices 4095-4096
  Legacy (raw slice): 4096 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 4095 chars — ✅ CLEAN, clipped=true

── Test 3: appendPreviewPart() scan cap (max=4096) ──
  Input: 4101 chars, emoji at indices 4095-4096
  Legacy (raw slice): 4096 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 4095 chars — ✅ CLEAN

── Test 4: truncateForGateway() title cap (max=80) ──
  Input: 82 chars, emoji at indices 76-77
  Legacy (raw slice): 80 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 79 chars — ✅ CLEAN

── Test 5: truncateForGateway() description cap (max=256) ──
  Input: 258 chars, emoji at indices 252-253
  Legacy (raw slice): 256 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 255 chars — ✅ CLEAN

── Test 6: truncateDisplayText() param value cap (max=120) ──
  Input: 122 chars, emoji at indices 116-117
  Legacy (raw slice): 120 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 119 chars — ✅ CLEAN

── Test 7: sanitizeDisplayText() scan cap (max=4096) ──
  (boundary-lucky case: old code clean, safe slice also clean — correct either way)
  (boundary-unlucky case: emoji at 4095-4096)
  Legacy (raw slice): 4096 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 4095 chars — ✅ CLEAN

── Test 8: truncate() permission value cap (max=48) ──
  Legacy (raw slice): 48 chars — ❌ LONE SURROGATE
  Fixed (utf16-safe): 47 chars — ✅ CLEAN

── Test 9: boundary variants ──
  PASS emoji at prefix, at end, after slice — all clean

======================================================================
RESULT: 0/18 failures
======================================================================

✅ PROOF PASSED — all truncation paths produce clean UTF-16

Coverage: 9 tests × 6 call sites × 3 source files
  - approval-bridge.ts: truncate(), previewSource(), appendPreviewPart()
  - elicitation-bridge.ts: sanitizeDisplayText(), truncateDisplayText()
  - plugin-approval-roundtrip.ts: truncateForGateway()
```

### 2. Unit tests (Vitest) — 115 passed

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/approval-bridge.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/elicitation-bridge.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

These exercise `handleCodexAppServerApprovalRequest` and `handleCodexAppServerElicitationRequest` (the real entry points) with the full `buildApprovalContext` → all truncation helpers pipeline. The 2 new regression tests assert zero lone surrogates in the approval events and gateway request payloads that would reach the user.

### 3. Lint / format / review

- `oxlint` on all 5 changed files — **clean** (2 pre-existing errors in unchanged test lines fixed in follow-up `742aec8`)
- `oxfmt --check` — **clean**
- Autoreview: **no findings**

### 4. Codex environment

- `codex` v0.142.5 installed globally — the app-server binary is present and would exercise these paths
- **Not authenticated** (no `codex login`) and API endpoints blocked by corporate firewall → cannot record a live roundtrip

### Summary

| Evidence Layer | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Standalone proof script | 6 call sites, 18 boundary tests, old-vs-new comparison | **0/18 failures** |
| Vitest unit tests | 115 tests, real handler entry points + full truncation pipeline | **115 passed** |
| oxlint | Changed files | **clean** |
| Autoreview | Full PR diff | **no findings** |

Behavior addressed: the `truncate()` / `previewSource()` / `appendPreviewPart()` / `sanitizeDisplayText()` / `truncateDisplayText()` / `truncateForGateway()` helpers used for codex approval and elicitation preview text.

Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/codex-utf16-safe-truncation`, commit `742aec8`. Codex 0.142.5 installed but unauthenticated (API blocked).

Observed result after fix: proof script and unit tests independently verify that old raw-slice code produced lone surrogates in 6 of 9 tested boundary positions; the fix produces clean UTF-16 in all cases.

What was not tested: real Codex app-server end-to-end roundtrip with a live LLM that produces emoji in command previews — blocked by missing Codex auth and corporate API firewall on this machine. The proof script and unit tests together cover every truncation call site with exact emoji-boundary inputs and verify the output has zero lone surrogates.
